key_insight: Encoding conditions in the input state lets one shared IQP circuit represent conditional distributions beyond those achievable by diagonal conditioning with the same qubit count.
engineering_relevance: This approach enables classical training of conditional quantum generative models without requiring quantum hardware during optimization.
method: Encode each condition in the input state while sharing a single IQP unitary.
Use efficient reference-state sampling and amplitude-ratio evaluation to estimate conditional maximum mean discrepancy and its gradients without bias.
Train against conditional Curie–Weiss spin distributions.
evidence_signal: On a 16-qubit Curie–Weiss benchmark, mean total variation distance was six times lower than diagonal conditioning at held-out temperatures; models up to 2048 qubits reproduced mean squared magnetization away from the crossover.
watch_item: Classical training requires efficient reference-state sampling and amplitude-ratio evaluation, and the reported large-scale results do not establish full-distribution accuracy or quantum advantage.
paper_title: Classical training of conditional instantaneous quantum polynomial-time Born machines
